we have developed the first approximation algorithms to find a B term wavelets representation of a given function that provable approximates its best representation under a wide variety and generalizations of lp norms.

(i) the wavelet transform coding problem with a fixed basis and general lp distance is polynomially solvable for Haar wavelets, and (ii) the wavelet basis selection problem can be solved by a polynomially solvable algorithm for the Haar wavelet transform coding problems.

the problem of finding the best representation in the lp norm for a discrete signal can be solved in sublinear space in the number of data points, and in polynomial time for a wide variety of bases, and that this problem can be extended to finding the best representation under a universal dictionary of bases, and to the bit budget problem.

the following questions: (i) How well does a B term representation using a wavelet basis approximate an unknown function f, (ii) How well does it approximate a given function f, and (iii) What is the best basis for a given function f?

the problem of finding the optimal B term representation of a function under general lp distance measures is computationally hard.
